children: Just weeks after the Bitcoin whitepaper turned 18, a forgotten forum created by Satoshi Nakamoto is drawing fresh attention. A post on X has sparked a lively debate about it.
Its admin account logged in again in 2014. That detail deepens the long mystery around Bitcoin’s anonymous creator.
How Satoshi’s Forgotten Bitcoin Forum Drew Attention
ZetaBoards was a free service that let anyone launch an online forum. In November 2009, Satoshi used it to create a board simply called Bitcoin.
At the time, Bitcoin was barely a year old.
on October 31, 2008, and was now searching for a home for its tiny community.
However, this forum never became the main hub.
Days later, Satoshi opened a forum on bitcoin.org, which later became BitcoinTalk.
The forum drew attention after crypto enthusiast Sean Murray shared an archived copy of the page on X. His post quickly sparked debate. The Wayback Machine had saved that snapshot in June 2018.

image.alt: Satoshi Nakamoto’s Lost Bitcoin Forum Sparks a 2014 Mystery. Source: WayBack Machine

children: The snapshot shows just three members, and each held administrator rights. The “satoshi” account joined on November 13, 2009, and left five posts. It was last active on November 21, 2009.
Meanwhile, “sirius-m” registered on November 15 but never posted. The third account, “admin,” joined on November 14, 2009. Surprisingly, it last logged in on June 17, 2014.
Who Logged Into Satoshi’s Forum in 2014?
Murray offered a partial answer. He shared a November 14, 2009 email from Satoshi to Martti Malmi, one of Bitcoin’s earliest developers.
In it, Satoshi explained that InvisionFree was moving to ZetaBoards, so he had set up a forum there. He then sent Malmi the admin login and password.
The dates match perfectly. The admin account appeared the same day as the email, and Malmi has long used the “sirius-m” nickname. Still, at least two people knew the admin password.
As a result, nobody can say for sure who logged in back in 2014.
That uncertainty fits a much larger puzzle. Eighteen years after the whitepaper,
. Over time, theories have pointed to cypherpunks such as Hal Finney, Nick Szabo, and Adam Back.
In 2024, the HBO documentary Money Electric suggested developer Peter Todd, who denied the claim. That same year, a UK court ruled that Craig Wright is not Satoshi.
Now, another twist has emerged. Charlie Shrem, an early Bitcoin entrepreneur, recently claimed that researchers traced Satoshi through several fictional names.
According to Shrem, Satoshi never left the community and kept talking under other pseudonyms.
However, the group does not plan to reveal his identity.

title: Satoshi Nakamoto’s Forgotten Bitcoin Forum Reveals a 2014 Mystery
